sections.h2: Where do McLean County owners go with a tax question?
sections.html:
If the question is about value, go to the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA); if it is about paying, go to the Sheriff. The PVA takes letters at P.O. Box 246, Calhoun, KY 42327, and answers calls at (270) 273-3291. The Sheriff's Office occupies 135 East 2nd Street in Calhoun, and the Sheriff's page on the county website carries a link to online property tax records.

They run as separate counters. January 1 values and exemption forms belong to the PVA, which cannot accept a payment. The Sheriff accepts money through April 15 and then passes what is left to the County Clerk. A house in Calhoun, Livermore, Island, Sacramento or open country answers to the same two.

sections.h2: How fast do penalties grow on a McLean County bill?
sections.html:
The ladder comes from KRS 134.015. Paying everything by November 1 saves 2 percent, and 2026's date is behind us. From there:

  • The rest of the year: the printed amount.
  • January: 5 percent extra.
  • After January: 10 percent extra.
  • April 15 ends the Sheriff's role, and open bills move to the County Clerk.

If mailing runs late, the state revenue department may switch to a slower schedule of one month each at discount, face value and the 5 percent penalty. Under either schedule the unpaid tax is the taxpayer's own debt, backdated to the assessment date.

sections.h2: What might a McLean County owner expect to pay?
sections.html:
Multiply the Census median of $148,500 by 10.6 cents per $100, the 2025 state rate, and the state's piece is about $157.41. The fiscal court, the school district and other taxing bodies add rates of their own, so ask the PVA for a total on any given address.

The county has been losing people for a century, which limits how many buyers are around. Wikipedia lists the census counts:

Census QuickFacts estimates 9,064 people in 2025 and counts 3,641 households. Owners live in 82.8 percent of the homes, rent runs $641 at the median, and two building permits in 2025 mean a sale is nearly always an existing house.

sections.h2: Can McLean County owners claim a homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Yes, as in every county. A deduction of $49,100 from assessed value covers 2025 and 2026 for anyone 65 or older and anyone found totally disabled. With 22.5 percent of residents at 65 or older, plenty of households fit.

Run the median house through it and $99,400 stays taxable, so the state's slice is about $105.36. The PVA takes the application along with a driver's license, birth certificate or passport. Disability claims need a government or pension finding and a yearly renewal, apart from service-connected veterans and people already ruled permanent and total by Social Security or the Kentucky Retirement Systems. Once the house sells, tell the PVA so the deduction leaves the old address.

sections.h2: How does a McLean County owner challenge a valuation?
sections.html:
Book a meeting with the PVA first, since the board of assessment appeals takes only owners who had one.

  • The roll is open for 13 days from the first Monday in May, with dates advertised in the county's largest newspaper.
  • In the meeting, the PVA explains your number and a form records what was said.
  • Deliver the appeal to the County Clerk before closing time on the business day after inspection ends.
  • Bring paper: land and building descriptions, insurance records, construction costs, and listings or sales of similar property. Bare claims are rejected.

The board sits about a month later and owes you written reasons for any change. Paid representatives must come from the state's list of professions and show your written authority. Skip the hearing and the Kentucky Claims Commission is off the table.

sections.h2: What happens to McLean County taxes still owed at closing?
sections.html:
A lien follows the parcel and does not care who sells it. The County Clerk holds bills still open after April 15 as certificates of delinquency, records the lien, and begins charging 1 percent a month. Under KRS 134.420 the lien survives 11 years, whoever owns the house next.

Costs stack in layers: 10 percent for the Clerk, 20 percent for the county attorney once notices go out, plus postage, advertising and lien fees. The revenue department's own example turns a $1,000 bill into a $1,254 certificate before any of those. Ask the Sheriff for a payoff until April 15 and the Clerk afterward. A certificate can be auctioned 90 to 135 days after the transfer, and the buyer may add charges.

sections.h2: What is McLean County like for someone selling a home?
sections.html:
McLean County was carved out on February 6, 1854, from parts of Daviess, Ohio and Muhlenberg counties. Its 256 square miles lie in the Western Coal Fields, inside the Owensboro metropolitan area. The Green River crosses the county from southeast to northwest, with bridges at Calhoun and Livermore and a Corps of Engineers lock and dam, No. 2, at Calhoun. McLean is a dry county where alcohol sales are prohibited.

Calhoun is the seat and Livermore the largest community; Island and Sacramento are also cities. A single county-wide school district runs the high school and middle school, both east of Calhoun on Highway 136, and elementaries in Calhoun, Livermore and Sacramento. Schools at Beech Grove and Island closed long ago. The county is served by a weekly paper, the McLean County News, and sits in the Owensboro radio market. Clocks follow Central time.

Commutes average 31.4 minutes, median household income is $65,596, and 15.8 percent of people live in poverty. Six counties border McLean: Henderson, Daviess, Ohio, Muhlenberg, Hopkins and Webster. A high school diploma is held by 91.7 percent of adults 25 and over, and 85.3 percent of households have broadband for looking up a bill or exemption form. Anyone with an inherited house, a rural parcel or tax still owing can sell for cash as-is. Collect the payoff from the Sheriff and the parcel record from the PVA before naming a price.

The local economy is small. Census business data list 161 employer establishments with 947 employees and a $40 million payroll in 2023, and retail sales of about $92.5 million in 2022. Employment fell 2.7 percent between 2022 and 2023. Wikipedia estimates that 350 to 400 residents are enrolled in some form of higher education at any moment, and the Census counts 430 veterans in the county. With the mean commute at 31.4 minutes, many working residents likely travel outside the county, and the Owensboro metropolitan area is the nearest large job base. Ask the Sheriff, the PVA and the County Clerk each for their piece of the paper trail before you set a closing date, since each office holds a different record on the same parcel.

faqs.q: Does the McLean County PVA take payments?
faqs.a: No. Call the PVA at (270) 273-3291 about assessments and exemptions, and pay the Sheriff.

faqs.q: When does a McLean County bill turn delinquent?
faqs.a: The 10 percent penalty starts when January ends. After April 15 the County Clerk gets any open bill, adds a lien and begins monthly interest of 1 percent.

faqs.q: What is the McLean County homestead exemption worth?
faqs.a: It cuts $49,100 from assessed value for 2025 and 2026. People 65 or older, or totally disabled, apply with the PVA in Calhoun.

faqs.q: What would the state collect on a median McLean County home?
faqs.a: Around $157.41 on the $148,500 Census median, using the state's 2025 rate of 10.6 cents per $100. Other levies are separate.

faqs.q: Who decides a McLean County assessment appeal?
faqs.a: A local board made up of area property owners. It meets about a month after the roll inspection, and you file through the County Clerk once you have seen the PVA.
